title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: In ε-Keggin molybdate microporous frameworks, heating can remove water and ammonia from zigzag micropores without framework collapse, and the resulting guest loss increases O2 uptake while Mo redox responds to H2 or O2.
explanation: Na–Mo–Mn and NH4–Mo–Fe, built from ε-Keggin {MMo12} units and transition-metal linkers, retain their structures after calcination that partially clears micropores. Reported BET areas are about 22 and 20 m2 g−1. NH4–Mo–Fe shows temperature-dependent O2 adsorption because higher temperature expels more water and NH3 and opens micropores; heating in H2 or O2 changes Mo valence.
scope: ε-Keggin polyoxomolybdate all-inorganic frameworks Na–Mo–Mn and NH4–Mo–Fe.
conditions: Hydrothermal synthesis near 175 °C; N2 sorption after calcination; O2 isotherms under normal pressure; redox heating in H2 or O2.
caveats: Surface areas are low, and pore cleaning is described as partial. The redox and sorption behavior is reported for this pair of frameworks, not for all POMo frameworks.
